Big picture: Biology Builds From Small To Big — molecules → cells → tissues → organs → systems → organisms. Units 1–3 (molecular/cellular) are the foundation everything else depends on.

blocks.title: Review schedule
items: Daily: 15–20 min on current unit notes
Weekly: practice questions — if you can't answer them, you don't know the material
Bi-weekly: revisit old units
Before exams: focus on how units connect

blocks.title: Reality check
items: Systems units build on each other — digestive needs circulatory needs respiratory, etc. Falling behind in Bio 12 is brutal to recover from.

blocks.text: Definition: body maintaining internal balance despite external changes.
Mechanism: negative feedback loops — Receptors detect change → Control center processes → Effectors respond.
Examples: temperature regulation, blood glucose control, pH balance.

items: Polar molecule, partial charges; covalent bonds within, hydrogen bonds between molecules
Solvent, temperature moderator (high specific heat, evaporative cooling), cohesion/adhesion, transport medium
0–6 acidic, 7 neutral, 8–14 basic
Acids release H⁺, bases release OH⁻
Buffers resist pH change — crucial for enzyme function
Blood pH ≈ 7.4, stomach pH ≈ 2

blocks.title: Macromolecule cheat sheet
steps: Carbohydrates — monomers: monosaccharides; quick energy, structural support, energy storage
Lipids — triglycerides (long-term energy, insulation), phospholipids (membranes), steroids (hormones)
Proteins — monomers: amino acids; primary → secondary → tertiary structure; shape determines function
Nucleic acids — DNA/RNA, nucleotides (phosphate + sugar + base); store/transmit genetic info; ATP = energy currency

blocks.title: Memory hacks
items: CLPN — Carbs quick energy, Lipids long-term, Proteins do work, Nucleic acids store info
Organelles: "Never Call My Rough English, Go Learn Coding" (Nucleus, Cytoplasm, Mitochondria, Ribosomes, ER, Golgi, Lysosomes, Chloroplasts)
All living things are made of cells
Cells are the basic unit of life
All cells come from pre-existing cells

blocks.text: Prokaryotes: no nucleus, less efficient (bacteria). Eukaryotes: have nucleus, more efficient (plants, animals).

ER — transport (rough has ribosomes)

modules.title: Animal only
items: Lysosomes — digest waste

modules.title: Plant only

Cell wall — structure/protection
Large vacuole — storage/support

blocks.text: Passive (no energy): diffusion, osmosis, facilitated diffusion.
Active (requires energy): primary (ATP direct), secondary (gradients), endocytosis, exocytosis.
Tonicity: isotonic — no net movement; hypertonic — cell shrinks; hypotonic — cell swells.

blocks.title: Memory hacks
items: "Water follows salt" for osmosis
"HYPE-rtonic makes cells shrink from HYPE-rdehydration"

blocks.title: Foundation warning
items: If you don't understand transport, every other unit gets harder — this connects to everything.
Double helix; base pairing A-T, C-G; phosphate + deoxyribose + nitrogenous base
Semi-conservative replication: Helicase unzips, DNA polymerase adds nucleotides, Ligase seals fragments

blocks.text: RNA differs from DNA: single strand, ribose sugar, uracil instead of thymine. Types: mRNA (messenger), tRNA (transfer), rRNA (ribosomal).

blocks.title: Central dogma
steps: Transcription (nucleus): RNA polymerase reads DNA template → mRNA
Translation (ribosomes): Initiation → Elongation (tRNA brings amino acids) → Termination (stop codon, protein released)

blocks.text: Point mutations: silent (no effect), missense (different amino acid), nonsense (premature stop). Frameshift: insertion/deletion shifts reading frame.

items: Biological catalysts, lower activation energy; lock-and-key active site
Affected by temperature (denaturation past optimum), pH, concentration
Inhibition: competitive (competes for active site) vs non-competitive (binds elsewhere, changes shape)

blocks.title: Memory hacks
items: Base pairs: "Apple Tree, Car Garage" (A-T, C-G)
Central dogma: "DNA makes RNA makes Protein" (DRP)
Replication: "Helicase Helps, Polymerase Produces, Ligase Links"
Restaurant analogy: DNA = recipe book, mRNA = order ticket, tRNA = waiters, ribosome = kitchen

blocks.text: Pathway: Mouth → Esophagus → Stomach → Small intestine → Large intestine → Rectum.

items: Mechanical digestion: physical breakdown (chewing, churning)
Chemical digestion: enzyme breakdown — amylase (starch), pepsin (protein), lipase (fats)
Absorption mainly in small intestine, optimized via villi

blocks.title: Memory hack
items: "My Mouth Eats Small Lunch Regularly" — trace the pathway first, then layer in enzymes/absorption.
External respiration: gas exchange in lungs (O₂ in, CO₂ out)
Internal respiration: gas exchange at tissues
Alveoli: tiny air sacs for gas exchange; hemoglobin carries O₂
Medulla monitors CO₂ levels and adjusts breathing rate

blocks.title: Memory hack
items: BRIN — Breathe, Ribs expand, Internal gas exchange, Nose/mouth entry.
Heart: 2 atria (receive blood), 2 ventricles (pump blood)
Blood flow: right side → lungs → left side → body
Arteries: away from heart, thick walls, high pressure. Veins: return to heart, valves, lower pressure. Capillaries: thin walls, gas/nutrient exchange
Blood: RBCs (O₂ transport), WBCs (immune), platelets (clotting), plasma (liquid)

blocks.title: Memory hacks
items: "Right Ventricle Leaves, Left Ventricle Arrives"; "Arteries Away, Veins Venture back".
CNS: brain and spinal cord. PNS: all other nerves
Neurons: electrical signals within cell, chemical signals between cells
Reflexes: automatic protective responses
Brain processes sensory info and controls responses

Filters blood, removes wastes, maintains water/salt balance
Nephrons: functional units of kidneys
Process: Filtration → Reabsorption → Secretion → Excretion
Hormones: ADH (water retention), aldosterone (salt retention)

blocks.title: Memory hack

Male: testes produce sperm and testosterone
Female: ovaries produce eggs, estrogen, progesterone
Menstrual cycle: hormone-controlled monthly cycle
Fertilization in fallopian tube; development: embryo → fetus → baby

cards.q: Trace the pathway of a negative feedback loop.
cards.a: Stimulus → receptor → control center → effector → response

cards.q: Why is water a good solvent?
cards.a: It's polar, so it dissolves polar/ionic substances

cards.q: What's the difference between passive and active transport?
cards.a: Passive needs no energy (diffusion, osmosis, facilitated diffusion); active requires ATP

cards.q: What happens to a cell in a hypertonic solution?
cards.a: It shrinks — water leaves the cell

cards.q: Name the 3 enzymes in DNA replication.
cards.a: Helicase (unzips), DNA polymerase (adds nucleotides), Ligase (seals fragments)

cards.q: Where do transcription and translation happen?
cards.a: Transcription in the nucleus; translation at ribosomes in the cytoplasm

cards.q: What's the digestive pathway in order?
cards.a: Mouth → esophagus → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → rectum

cards.q: What are the heart's 4 chambers and their roles?
cards.a: 2 atria receive blood, 2 ventricles pump blood
